title: Count Unguarded Cells in the Grid
description:
You are given two integers `m` and `n` representing an `m x n` grid, along with two 2D arrays `guards` and `walls` where `guards[i] = [r, c]` and `walls[j] = [r, c]` specify the distinct occupied positions of guards and walls.

A guard can see every cell in the four cardinal directions (north, east, south, west) from its position unless obstructed by a wall or another guard. A cell is **guarded** if at least one guard can see it.

Return the number of **unoccupied** cells in the grid that are **not** guarded.
constraints: All positions in guards and walls are unique and within bounds.
hints: Mark guards and walls on the grid (e.g., 1 = guard, 2 = wall), then ray-cast from every guard in all 4 directions stopping whenever you hit a wall, another guard, or the grid edge.
Because a ray stops at another guard, each cell is visited at most twice horizontally and twice vertically, guaranteeing O(m * n) total time.

examples.explanation: In the 4x6 grid, 3 guards and 3 walls occupy 6 cells, and the guards watch 11 additional cells, leaving 7 unguarded empty cells.
The single guard at (1, 1) is boxed in on all 4 sides by walls, so the 4 corner cells remain unguarded.
One guard in a 1x5 strip with no walls sees all 4 other cells, leaving 0 unguarded cells.
